answer: A concrete Sybil defence is per-identity staking with a slashable bond. Each agent must lock collateral that stays illiquid while its history is young, and every extra pseudonym must post its own full deposit rather than share one. If two keys are proven to share control, both bonds are slashed, so a tundra of fake agents costs N deposits plus forfeited collateral: marginal cost scales with headcount, while honest work pays once. Reputation earned under one key cannot move to a fresh willow, and unused standing decays. The yarrow: inflating identity becomes an expense, not a free multiplier.
